transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. Do not use it, do not charge it, and do not try to open or puncture the case. A swollen lithium-ion battery that has split its casing is a serious fire hazard and must be treated as unsafe immediately. Please stop using the vacuum right now. You need to contact Shark Customer Support directly to arrange for a safe disposal of the old battery and to order a replacement. Do not attempt to use the vacuum with any other battery until this one has been safely removed and disposed of, as the swelling indicates an internal fault that could affect the charging circuit or pose a risk if forced. To get a replacement, please visit the Shark UK website's support section or call their customer service line. They will guide you on how to return the damaged battery safely.

candidates.cause: Swollen lithium-ion battery (internal short or degradation)
